TITLE: Heart Failure Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Heart Failure Discharge Instructions. Weigh yourself every morning after you use the bathroom and before breakfast. Write the number down. Call the heart failure clinic if your weight goes up more than 2 pounds in one day or more than 5 pounds in one week.

TITLE: Heart Failure Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Heart Failure Discharge Instructions. Limit sodium to 2,000 mg per day. Read food labels, skip canned soups and deli meats, and do not add salt at the table. Limit all fluids to 2 liters (about 8 cups) per day unless your cardiologist gives you a different number.

TITLE: Heart Failure Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Heart Failure Discharge Instructions. Take your water pill (furosemide) in the morning so you are not up all night. Bring every pill bottle to your first clinic visit.

TITLE: Heart Failure Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Heart Failure Discharge Instructions. Your first heart failure clinic visit should be within 7 days of discharge. Go to the emergency department if you are short of breath at rest or cannot lie flat to sleep.

TITLE: Heart Failure Clinic Medication Titration Protocol
CHUNK_TEXT: Heart Failure Clinic Medication Titration Protocol. Clinic pharmacists increase guideline-directed heart failure medicines one step at a time, no more often than every 2 weeks, when blood pressure and heart rate allow.

TITLE: Heart Failure Clinic Medication Titration Protocol
CHUNK_TEXT: Heart Failure Clinic Medication Titration Protocol. Check potassium and creatinine 1 to 2 weeks after starting or increasing spironolactone. Hold spironolactone and call the cardiologist if potassium is above 5.5 mmol/L.

TITLE: Heart Failure Clinic Medication Titration Protocol
CHUNK_TEXT: Heart Failure Clinic Medication Titration Protocol. Do not increase a beta blocker during a visit when the patient has signs of fluid overload such as new leg swelling or weight gain over 5 pounds.

TITLE: After Your Heart Stent (PCI) Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: After Your Heart Stent (PCI) Discharge Instructions. Do not stop aspirin or clopidogrel unless your cardiologist tells you to. Stopping these antiplatelet medicines early can cause the stent to clot. Plan on taking both for 12 months.

TITLE: After Your Heart Stent (PCI) Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: After Your Heart Stent (PCI) Discharge Instructions. If the catheter went in at your wrist, do not lift more than 5 pounds with that arm for 48 hours. A small bruise is normal. Hold firm pressure and call 911 if the site bleeds and does not stop.

TITLE: After Your Heart Stent (PCI) Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: After Your Heart Stent (PCI) Discharge Instructions. If you have chest pain, take one nitroglycerin under the tongue. If the pain is not better after 5 minutes, call 911.

TITLE: After Your Heart Stent (PCI) Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: After Your Heart Stent (PCI) Discharge Instructions. You will be referred to cardiac rehabilitation. Your first rehab session should be within 2 weeks of discharge.

TITLE: Warfarin Patient Education
CHUNK_TEXT: Warfarin Patient Education. Warfarin is a blood thinner. For atrial fibrillation, the usual INR target range is 2.0 to 3.0. Your clinic will tell you your own range.

TITLE: Warfarin Patient Education
CHUNK_TEXT: Warfarin Patient Education. You do not need to avoid leafy green vegetables. Keep the amount of vitamin K foods about the same from week to week so your INR stays steady.

TITLE: Warfarin Patient Education
CHUNK_TEXT: Warfarin Patient Education. Watch for bleeding: black or tarry stools, pink or red urine, nosebleeds that last more than 10 minutes, or unusual bruising. Call the anticoagulation clinic the same day.

TITLE: Warfarin Patient Education
CHUNK_TEXT: Warfarin Patient Education. After any dose change, your INR is checked again in 3 to 5 days.

TITLE: Anticoagulation Bridging Protocol for Surgery
CHUNK_TEXT: Anticoagulation Bridging Protocol for Surgery. For high-risk patients on warfarin who need surgery, stop warfarin 5 days before the procedure.

TITLE: Anticoagulation Bridging Protocol for Surgery
CHUNK_TEXT: Anticoagulation Bridging Protocol for Surgery. Start enoxaparin 1 mg/kg every 12 hours 3 days before surgery. Give the last enoxaparin dose 24 hours before the procedure.

TITLE: Anticoagulation Bridging Protocol for Surgery
CHUNK_TEXT: Anticoagulation Bridging Protocol for Surgery. Restart warfarin the evening after surgery if the surgeon agrees. For low bleeding-risk procedures, resume enoxaparin 24 hours after surgery until the INR is in range.

TITLE: COPD Exacerbation Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: COPD Exacerbation Discharge Instructions. Take prednisone 40 mg once a day with breakfast for 5 days, then stop. Do not taper unless your doctor says so.

TITLE: COPD Exacerbation Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: COPD Exacerbation Discharge Instructions. Use your inhalers exactly as the respiratory therapist showed you. Bring them to every visit so the team can check your technique with teach-back.

TITLE: COPD Exacerbation Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: COPD Exacerbation Discharge Instructions. Use your COPD action plan. Green zone: usual breathing. Yellow zone: more cough, mucus or shortness of breath, start your rescue plan and call the clinic. Red zone: trouble talking or blue lips, call 911.

TITLE: COPD Exacerbation Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: COPD Exacerbation Discharge Instructions. You are referred to pulmonary rehabilitation. Start within 4 weeks of discharge.

TITLE: Home Oxygen Safety
CHUNK_TEXT: Home Oxygen Safety. Never smoke or let anyone smoke in a room where oxygen is used. Keep oxygen at least 6 feet away from open flames, gas stoves and candles.

TITLE: Home Oxygen Safety
CHUNK_TEXT: Home Oxygen Safety. Store oxygen tanks upright and secured in a stand or cart so they cannot fall over. Keep them out of hot cars and away from heaters.

TITLE: Home Oxygen Safety
CHUNK_TEXT: Home Oxygen Safety. Oxygen tubing can be up to 50 feet long. Tape it along walls to lower the chance of tripping.

TITLE: Adult Asthma Action Plan Education
CHUNK_TEXT: Adult Asthma Action Plan Education. If you need your rescue inhaler more than 2 days a week, your asthma is not well controlled. Tell your doctor at your next visit.

TITLE: Adult Asthma Action Plan Education
CHUNK_TEXT: Adult Asthma Action Plan Education. Rinse your mouth with water and spit after each dose of your steroid inhaler to prevent thrush.

TITLE: Adult Asthma Action Plan Education
CHUNK_TEXT: Adult Asthma Action Plan Education. Go to the emergency department if your rescue inhaler does not help within 20 minutes or you have trouble walking or talking.

TITLE: Community-Acquired Pneumonia Care Protocol
CHUNK_TEXT: Community-Acquired Pneumonia Care Protocol. Switch from IV to oral antibiotics when the patient has been clinically stable for 24 hours and can take pills by mouth.

TITLE: Community-Acquired Pneumonia Care Protocol
CHUNK_TEXT: Community-Acquired Pneumonia Care Protocol. Treat for at least 5 days in total. Stop only when the patient has had no fever for 48 hours and no more than one sign of instability.

TITLE: Community-Acquired Pneumonia Care Protocol
CHUNK_TEXT: Community-Acquired Pneumonia Care Protocol. A follow-up chest x-ray at 6 to 8 weeks is recommended only for patients over 50 or current smokers, to rule out an underlying mass.

TITLE: Sepsis Early Management Bundle
CHUNK_TEXT: Sepsis Early Management Bundle. Measure a lactate level within 1 hour of suspected sepsis. Repeat it within 6 hours if the first lactate is above 2 mmol/L.

TITLE: Sepsis Early Management Bundle
CHUNK_TEXT: Sepsis Early Management Bundle. Draw blood cultures before giving the first dose of broad-spectrum antibiotics, but do not delay antibiotics more than 45 minutes waiting for cultures.

TITLE: Sepsis Early Management Bundle
CHUNK_TEXT: Sepsis Early Management Bundle. Give 30 mL/kg of IV crystalloid fluid for low blood pressure or a lactate of 4 mmol/L or higher.

TITLE: Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) Isolation Policy
CHUNK_TEXT: Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) Isolation Policy. Place patients with suspected or confirmed C. diff on contact plus precautions: gown and gloves for every room entry and a dedicated stethoscope.

TITLE: Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) Isolation Policy
CHUNK_TEXT: Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) Isolation Policy. Clean hands with soap and water after care. Alcohol hand gel does not kill C. diff spores.

TITLE: Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) Isolation Policy
CHUNK_TEXT: Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) Isolation Policy. Isolation can stop 48 hours after diarrhea resolves. Clean the room with a bleach-based disinfectant at discharge.

TITLE: Hand Hygiene Policy
CHUNK_TEXT: Hand Hygiene Policy. Clean hands at the five moments: before touching a patient, before a clean or aseptic task, after body fluid exposure, after touching a patient, and after touching patient surroundings.

TITLE: Hand Hygiene Policy
CHUNK_TEXT: Hand Hygiene Policy. Artificial nails and nail extensions are not allowed for staff who give direct patient care.

TITLE: Hand Hygiene Policy
CHUNK_TEXT: Hand Hygiene Policy. Each unit is audited monthly. The compliance target is 95 percent, and results are posted on the unit quality board.

TITLE: Total Hip Replacement Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Total Hip Replacement Discharge Instructions. Follow your posterior hip precautions for 6 weeks: do not bend your hip past 90 degrees, do not cross your legs, and do not turn your foot inward.

TITLE: Total Hip Replacement Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Total Hip Replacement Discharge Instructions. To prevent blood clots, take aspirin 81 mg twice a day for 35 days after surgery.

TITLE: Total Hip Replacement Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Total Hip Replacement Discharge Instructions. Your staples will be removed at your clinic visit 10 to 14 days after surgery. Do not lift more than 10 pounds until your surgeon clears you.

TITLE: Total Hip Replacement Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Total Hip Replacement Discharge Instructions. Do not drive for at least 4 weeks and never while taking opioid pain medicine.

TITLE: Total Knee Replacement Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Total Knee Replacement Discharge Instructions. Your goal is to bend your new knee to 90 degrees within 2 weeks. Do the home exercises 3 times a day.

TITLE: Total Knee Replacement Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Total Knee Replacement Discharge Instructions. Ice your knee for 20 minutes at a time, several times a day, with a cloth between the ice and your skin.

TITLE: Total Knee Replacement Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Total Knee Replacement Discharge Instructions. Outpatient physical therapy is 3 times a week for 6 to 8 weeks.

TITLE: Total Knee Replacement Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Total Knee Replacement Discharge Instructions. Call your surgeon right away for new calf pain, calf swelling or a fever over 101 F.

TITLE: Cast Care at Home
CHUNK_TEXT: Cast Care at Home. Keep your cast dry. Cover it with a plastic bag to shower. Never push objects like coat hangers inside the cast to scratch.

TITLE: Cast Care at Home
CHUNK_TEXT: Cast Care at Home. Keep the injured arm or leg raised above the level of your heart for the first 48 to 72 hours to reduce swelling.

TITLE: Cast Care at Home
CHUNK_TEXT: Cast Care at Home. Call the clinic for numbness, tingling, toes or fingers that turn blue or cold, or pain that gets worse when you move them.

TITLE: Diabetes Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Diabetes Discharge Instructions. For low blood sugar under 70 mg/dL, use the rule of 15: take 15 grams of fast sugar such as 4 ounces of juice, then recheck in 15 minutes.

TITLE: Diabetes Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Diabetes Discharge Instructions. Check your blood sugar before each meal and at bedtime. Write the numbers in your log and bring it to clinic.

TITLE: Diabetes Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Diabetes Discharge Instructions. On sick days, keep taking your long-acting (basal) insulin even if you are not eating. Check your sugar every 4 hours.

TITLE: Diabetes Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Diabetes Discharge Instructions. See the endocrinology clinic within 2 weeks of discharge.

TITLE: Insulin Pen Storage and Use
CHUNK_TEXT: Insulin Pen Storage and Use. Store unopened insulin pens in the refrigerator. Do not freeze them, and throw away any pen that has been frozen.

TITLE: Insulin Pen Storage and Use
CHUNK_TEXT: Insulin Pen Storage and Use. An insulin pen you are using can stay at room temperature for up to 28 days. Write the date you opened it on the label.

TITLE: Insulin Pen Storage and Use
CHUNK_TEXT: Insulin Pen Storage and Use. Use a new pen needle for every injection and put used needles in a sharps container.

TITLE: Inpatient Hypoglycemia Treatment Protocol
CHUNK_TEXT: Inpatient Hypoglycemia Treatment Protocol. Treat any blood glucose below 70 mg/dL. If the patient can swallow, give 15 grams of fast-acting carbohydrate.

TITLE: Inpatient Hypoglycemia Treatment Protocol
CHUNK_TEXT: Inpatient Hypoglycemia Treatment Protocol. If the patient cannot swallow safely, give dextrose 50 percent 25 mL IV, or glucagon 1 mg IM if there is no IV access.

TITLE: Inpatient Hypoglycemia Treatment Protocol
CHUNK_TEXT: Inpatient Hypoglycemia Treatment Protocol. Recheck glucose every 15 minutes until it is above 100 mg/dL. Notify the provider for any value below 40 mg/dL.

TITLE: Fall Prevention Policy (2025 version, superseded)
CHUNK_TEXT: Fall Prevention Policy (2025 version, superseded). Score every patient with the Morse Fall Scale on admission and every shift. A score of 45 or higher means high fall risk.

TITLE: Fall Prevention Policy (2025 version, superseded)
CHUNK_TEXT: Fall Prevention Policy (2025 version, superseded). High fall risk patients get a bed alarm, a yellow wristband and hourly rounding.

TITLE: Fall Prevention Policy (2026 version)
CHUNK_TEXT: Fall Prevention Policy (2026 version). Score every patient with the Morse Fall Scale on admission, every shift and after any fall. A score of 50 or higher means high fall risk.

TITLE: Fall Prevention Policy (2026 version)
CHUNK_TEXT: Fall Prevention Policy (2026 version). High fall risk patients get a bed alarm, yellow non-slip socks, a yellow wristband and rounding every hour while awake and every 2 hours overnight.

TITLE: Fall Prevention Policy (2026 version)
CHUNK_TEXT: Fall Prevention Policy (2026 version). After any fall, hold a post-fall huddle on the unit within 1 hour and file a safety event report before the end of the shift.

TITLE: Pressure Injury Prevention Protocol
CHUNK_TEXT: Pressure Injury Prevention Protocol. A Braden Scale score of 18 or lower means the patient is at risk for pressure injury.

TITLE: Pressure Injury Prevention Protocol
CHUNK_TEXT: Pressure Injury Prevention Protocol. Reposition at-risk patients at least every 2 hours. Float the heels off the bed with a pillow under the calves.

TITLE: Pressure Injury Prevention Protocol
CHUNK_TEXT: Pressure Injury Prevention Protocol. Inspect the skin over the sacrum, heels and elbows at least once each shift and document any redness that does not fade with pressure.

TITLE: Discharge Medication Reconciliation Policy
CHUNK_TEXT: Discharge Medication Reconciliation Policy. A pharmacist reviews the discharge medication list for every patient taking 10 or more medicines, and for every patient on an anticoagulant or insulin.

TITLE: Discharge Medication Reconciliation Policy
CHUNK_TEXT: Discharge Medication Reconciliation Policy. The meds-to-beds program delivers first fills to the bedside before discharge so patients leave with medicines in hand.

TITLE: Discharge Medication Reconciliation Policy
CHUNK_TEXT: Discharge Medication Reconciliation Policy. Any change from the home medication list must have a reason documented in the discharge summary.

TITLE: Post-Discharge Follow-up Call Protocol
CHUNK_TEXT: Post-Discharge Follow-up Call Protocol. A nurse calls every patient within 48 hours of discharge. Make up to 3 call attempts on different days before closing the outreach.

TITLE: Post-Discharge Follow-up Call Protocol
CHUNK_TEXT: Post-Discharge Follow-up Call Protocol. During the call, review warning signs, confirm the follow-up appointment and ask the patient to read back each medicine name.

TITLE: Post-Discharge Follow-up Call Protocol
CHUNK_TEXT: Post-Discharge Follow-up Call Protocol. Patients with a LACE readmission score of 10 or higher must have a primary care visit scheduled within 7 days of discharge.

TITLE: Transportation Assistance Policy
CHUNK_TEXT: Transportation Assistance Policy. Patients without a ride to a follow-up appointment can get a free ride voucher from case management.

TITLE: Transportation Assistance Policy
CHUNK_TEXT: Transportation Assistance Policy. Request the ride at least 24 hours before the appointment. Patients with Medicaid are first referred to the non-emergency medical transportation benefit.

TITLE: Stroke and TIA Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Stroke and TIA Discharge Instructions. Learn BE FAST: Balance loss, Eyes (vision change), Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech trouble, Time to call 911.

TITLE: Stroke and TIA Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Stroke and TIA Discharge Instructions. Your blood pressure goal is below 130/80. Check it at home every day and bring the log to your visits.

TITLE: Stroke and TIA Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Stroke and TIA Discharge Instructions. Take your statin every day, even if your cholesterol numbers look good.

TITLE: Stroke and TIA Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Stroke and TIA Discharge Instructions. See the neurology clinic within 2 weeks. Do not drive until your neurologist clears you.

TITLE: Seizure Safety at Home
CHUNK_TEXT: Seizure Safety at Home. Take showers instead of baths, and do not swim alone.

TITLE: Seizure Safety at Home
CHUNK_TEXT: Seizure Safety at Home. If a seizure lasts more than 5 minutes, or a second seizure starts before the person wakes up, call 911.

TITLE: Seizure Safety at Home
CHUNK_TEXT: Seizure Safety at Home. During a seizure, turn the person on their side, put something soft under their head, and never put anything in their mouth.

TITLE: Kidney-Friendly Eating (CKD Diet Education)
CHUNK_TEXT: Kidney-Friendly Eating (CKD Diet Education). Avoid pain relievers such as ibuprofen and naproxen. These NSAIDs can harm your kidneys. Acetaminophen is usually safer; ask your doctor.

TITLE: Kidney-Friendly Eating (CKD Diet Education)
CHUNK_TEXT: Kidney-Friendly Eating (CKD Diet Education). If your potassium is high, limit bananas, oranges, potatoes and tomatoes. Your dietitian will give you a daily target.

TITLE: Kidney-Friendly Eating (CKD Diet Education)
CHUNK_TEXT: Kidney-Friendly Eating (CKD Diet Education). Take your phosphate binder with meals, not on an empty stomach.

TITLE: Contrast Kidney Injury Prevention Protocol
CHUNK_TEXT: Contrast Kidney Injury Prevention Protocol. Check eGFR before giving IV contrast to inpatients. For eGFR below 30, give IV normal saline before and after the scan unless the patient has heart failure.

TITLE: Contrast Kidney Injury Prevention Protocol
CHUNK_TEXT: Contrast Kidney Injury Prevention Protocol. Hold metformin at the time of contrast and for 48 hours after the scan in patients with eGFR below 30, then recheck kidney function before restarting.

TITLE: Opioid Safety After Surgery
CHUNK_TEXT: Opioid Safety After Surgery. Do not drink alcohol or take sleeping pills or benzodiazepines while you take opioid pain medicine. The mix can slow or stop your breathing.

TITLE: Opioid Safety After Surgery
CHUNK_TEXT: Opioid Safety After Surgery. Opioids cause constipation. Take the stool softener you were prescribed and drink plenty of water.

TITLE: Opioid Safety After Surgery
CHUNK_TEXT: Opioid Safety After Surgery. Get rid of leftover opioid pills at a drug take-back site or pharmacy drop box. Ask about a naloxone kit to keep at home.

TITLE: Surgical Wound Care Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Surgical Wound Care Discharge Instructions. You may shower 48 hours after surgery. Do not soak in a bath, hot tub or pool for 2 weeks.

TITLE: Surgical Wound Care Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Surgical Wound Care Discharge Instructions. The thin tape strips over your incision will fall off on their own in 7 to 10 days. Do not pull them off.

TITLE: Surgical Wound Care Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Surgical Wound Care Discharge Instructions. Call your surgeon for redness that spreads, yellow or green drainage, or a fever over 101 F.

TITLE: Postpartum Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Postpartum Discharge Instructions. Call your provider or go to the emergency department if you soak through a pad in an hour or pass clots bigger than an egg.

TITLE: Postpartum Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Postpartum Discharge Instructions. If you had high blood pressure during pregnancy, get a blood pressure check within 72 hours of going home.

TITLE: Postpartum Discharge Instructions
CHUNK_TEXT: Postpartum Discharge Instructions. Severe headache, vision changes or pain under the ribs after delivery can be signs of preeclampsia. Get care right away.

TITLE: Visitor Policy
CHUNK_TEXT: Visitor Policy. Up to 2 visitors may be at the bedside at one time. Quiet hours are 9 p.m. to 6 a.m.

TITLE: Visitor Policy
CHUNK_TEXT: Visitor Policy. Children under 12 must be with an adult who is not the patient.

TITLE: Interpreter Services Policy
CHUNK_TEXT: Interpreter Services Policy. Use a qualified medical interpreter for all clinical conversations with patients who prefer a language other than English. Do not use family members to interpret clinical information.

TITLE: Interpreter Services Policy
CHUNK_TEXT: Interpreter Services Policy. Phone and video interpreters are available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week through the interpreter line.
